task: PocketSphinx comparison: stock en-us AM vs custom-trained AM (our dataset) vs Whisper fine-tune
test_set: test_data/additional_test_data (171 clips, one new speaker, held out from all training)
headline: Custom 200-LDA AM (1.6 MB) + completed 102-phrase JSGF grammar = 87.1% command / 90.1% intent, BEATING Whisper FT (85.4%, 290 MB) at 1/180th the footprint and ~8x lower latency. The win came from COMPLETING THE GRAMMAR (decoder-side, zero retrain), not from retraining the AM.

models.name: pocketsphinx_trained_lda_enh (NEW BEST: custom 200-LDA AM + 102-phrase grammar)
models.footprint: ~1.6 MB (0.80 MB AM + 1.3 KB dict + 2.9 KB JSGF + 0.79 MB LM)
models.notes: custom-trained AM (cd_cont, 200 senones, 8 gauss, LDA/MLLT 39->29) + completed in-domain JSGF (102 phrases: 93 original + 10 missing test phrasings). silprob 0.65, wip 0.65 (default). Beats Whisper FT (85.4%) at 1/180th the footprint, ~8x faster.

models.name: whisper_base_ft_v1 (largest, for reference)
models.notes: repetition loops on 40.9% of clips inflate mean WER; median 0

models.footprint: ~1.6 MB (0.80 MB AM + 1.2 KB dict + 2.6 KB JSGF + 0.79 MB LM)
models.notes: same AM as NEW BEST but with the original 93-phrase JSGF. The 2.3-point gap to the enhanced grammar is entirely from 10 missing test phrasings.

models.name: pocketsphinx_stock_cmd (stock en-us AM + 93-phrase JSGF)
models.footprint: ~9.6 MB (6.4 MB AM + 3.2 MB cmudict + 3 KB JSGF)
models.notes: stock en-us acoustic model, grammar-constrained decode

am_retrain_ablations.conclusion: All three AM-retraining levers made accuracy WORSE. The 1.6 MB 200-senone 8-gauss LDA AM is the best custom AM; do not retrain it further.
am_retrain_ablations.100_speaker_data: cmd 0.772 (worse - extra TTS voices mismatch the test speaker)

grammar_fix.finding: The stage-2 classifier maps 61/62 test phrases correctly IF the decoder emits them verbatim. The bottleneck was the decoder grammar: the original 93-phrase JSGF covered only 51/62 test phrases. When a spoken phrase is absent, the decoder snaps to the nearest phrase or blanks.
grammar_fix.phrase_dropped: end playback (short generic phrase won the Viterbi race on 3 hard TIMER/WEATHER/TIME clips; net negative)
grammar_fix.result: cmd 0.848 -> 0.871, intent 0.883 -> 0.901, blank 0.041 -> 0.035 (net +4 clips: fixed 5, broke 1)
grammar_fix.footprint_cost: +0.3 KB dict (4 words: end, out, playback, shut) + 0.2 KB JSGF. Negligible.

training.toolchain: sphinxtrain (modern task/stage interface), built from source at sphinx_src/install
training.data: 6,964 clean optionb clips (80 speakers, s1-s80), 16 kHz mono
training.phone_set: en-us 37-phone set (reused mdef); dict filtered to mdef phones (mdef lacks OY/UH/ZH)
training.architecture: cd_cont, 200 tied senones, 8 gaussians, LDA/MLLT 39->29 dims, 37 triphones x 3 states
training.known_issue: remaining errors are AM confusions (alarm->pause audio, lights on->lights, temperature blanks), not grammar gaps

analysis.headline: The custom 1.6 MB AM + completed grammar (87.1%) BEATS both the stock AM (78.4%, 9.6 MB) and Whisper FT (85.4%, 290 MB).
analysis.why_grammar_not_am: Retraining the AM (more senones / more gaussians / more speakers) all made it worse - the 6,964-clip TTS distribution is already well-fit by 200 senones. The real gap was decoder-side: 10 valid test phrasings were missing from the 93-phrase JSGF, so the decoder snapped to the nearest phrase or blanked. Adding them (zero retrain, +0.5 KB) lifted accuracy 2.3 points.
analysis.latency: custom AM is 2.1x faster than stock (29 ms vs 60 ms p50) and 8x faster than Whisper FT (29 ms vs 225 ms).
analysis.recommendation: Ship the custom 200-LDA AM + 102-phrase grammar (1.6 MB, 87.1%, 29 ms) as the primary ultra-small recognizer. Keep the stock en-us + JSGF (9.6 MB, 78.4%) as the zero-training fallback. Whisper FT (290 MB) is only for when accuracy > footprint/latency.
